messages.text: Ice on the path again. Are you taking the cane this morning?
Yes. I do not argue with ice anymore. January of 2024 settled that question. I slipped on my own driveway — right hip, bruised it badly. No fracture but I was laid up a week.
I remember. You called me from the floor.
Rob has the plow contract now. I would rather pay him $40 a storm than go through that again.
Mom, Marco was asking about your family background for the ancestry page he's been building. Was Grandma Elsa's maiden name German?

Grandma Elsa was Schmidt before she married. Mother's side were Schmidts from Ohio. Father's family were also German — the Meyers — though Grandpa Otto was the immigrant in that line. The English part comes in on Mother's great-grandmother, her maiden name was Whitmore.
So primarily German with a strain of English. Got it.
That's right. My mother always said we were mostly German with a little English lace at the edges. She thought that was funny.
Did you end up doing the January budget planning?
I do it every January, the second week, same as always. Spreadsheet on the computer, every category laid out for the year. Christmas gifts at $600, birthday gifts at $400. It was done by the 14th.
You are the most organized person I know.
I have done it every January since 1970. If you stop doing it you lose your footing.
Did you sleep okay, Mom? You seemed a little distant on Sunday.
I'm alright. I set out two cups again this morning without thinking. That still happens more than I'd like. I caught it when I went to fill the second one.
How long has it been? Nearly seven years and it still happens.

It may always happen. There's a thing about the house being quiet in a particular way when I'm the only one here. The hum went when he went, I've said that before. Some mornings I notice it more than others.
Are you having a harder stretch this week? The anniversary of the workshop day is coming up.

I noticed. February is still February. But last year after we cleaned out Harold's workshop — you came up and we spent two days — something actually shifted. That was the turning point. I carry that day differently now.
It was hard. But I'm glad we did it.
What gets you through the hard February mornings?
So am I. You stayed two nights and we sorted every shelf. I donated most of it to the Saline VFW workshop. The room is a proper room now.

The same things every day. The reading first thing. The walk. The garden when the ground allows. Three o'clock tea — I stop whatever I'm doing and I make the full pot. The knitting in the evenings. Morning prayer. It's not complicated. Keeping the day the same shape as yesterday keeps the feeling manageable.
That structure sounds like it really holds you.
It does. Harold always said I ran the house like a ship. I didn't see it as a complaint.
Checking in. The anniversary week is hard. How are you doing this morning?
About the same as yesterday. I made myself get up and make the oatmeal. That is about as far as I have gotten.
I am coming up tomorrow. I will stay through Wednesday. We do not have to do anything, just be in the house.
I would like that. It has been about ten days of this. I am not frightened of it — I know it passes. But I would like the company.
I know it passes too. You have never wanted pills for it and Dr. Nguyen has not pushed. But Linda at the senior center mentioned a social-work volunteer if you ever wanted to talk to someone.
I might. Next time it comes around. Right now I just need it to be Tuesday and not February.
Still on for 8 am? It is cold but the path is clear.
Yes but I may need to cut at the first loop. Both knees are unhappy this morning and I already took my Tylenol at 7:15.
We can do one loop. It is fine. Bring your cane if the ground is uneven.
Just the knees, not the hip today. I will manage without it.
If you need a ride to the senior center tonight I can pick you up. Gets dark before six now.
That would be kind of you. I do not drive after dark. I have not since the operations in 2022.
No problem. I will be out front at 6:45.
Thank you. The daytime I am fine but headlights coming at me are still tricky. Dr. Hoang said it may not fully resolve.
Are you using the cane today? The sidewalk still looked icy near the library.
I took it. I use it when the ground is uncertain. That is the rule I made for myself after last January.
No. Dry ground and I am fine without it. I am not ready for a walker. I do not need one.
How much did the furnace repair end up being?
$380. I paid it from the money market. Mike from Saline Heating had it done in under two hours.
That is what that fund is for. Are you going to put it back?
I am cutting the fabric order for the next two months and putting that back in. Should be whole by April.
Did you see that piece in the Ann Arbor News about the county clerk race shaping up? Apparently someone's already filed.
I did. I may well vote for whoever the sensible one is regardless of party. That office needs someone who actually knows how to run records.
You've always split the ticket on that one. Remember 2022?
I do. A good county clerk is a good county clerk. I haven't voted a straight ticket since 2008 and I don't intend to start now.
If you had to describe where you stood politically in one phrase what would it be?

I was a Rockefeller Republican for most of my adult life. Fiscally responsible, stay out of people's bedrooms, support civil rights, don't make government the enemy. That party doesn't exist anymore. I re-registered Independent in 2016 and that's where I've stayed.
A Rockefeller Republican sounds almost quaint now.
It was the sensible center at the time. I miss it.
The senior center is doing a tablet orientation on March 5th. Would you want to go?

I don't think so. I got my CGM working properly because you sat down with me and showed me how to read it. I got onto Zoom because Eleanor set it up on my laptop and stayed until I could do it myself. If the tablet class doesn't have someone I know leading it, I'll pass.
What if I came with you?
Then I'd go. You're the reason I understand half the things on this phone.
Mom can you FaceTime me when Lily calls? She wants to show you her track uniform.
Yes. What time? I need to make sure I am not at the senior center.
I will be here. My phone will be charged. Tell her I want to see the whole thing.
How did you end up as the senior center bookkeeper? You never really told me the full story.
They had a $40 discrepancy in 2021 and nobody could find it. I was at the table and offered to look. Transposed entry in an invoice from June. Found it in under an hour.
And that turned into the whole role?
Linda asked me the next week if I would stay on. I said I would try a month. That was five years ago.
Dave is doing Dry January again. Lasted two weeks. How do you handle not drinking? You make it look effortless.
I genuinely never started. Harold had a beer on Fridays and I would have a small glass of wine at Thanksgiving and maybe Christmas. That has been the sum total for sixty years.
That is remarkable. No willpower required.
Never smoked either. My parents did and I always said I would not. I kept that one.
Greg is trying to quit — he's on week three with the patches. Any advice from experience?

Your father did it cold. Not a patch, not a stick of gum. 1979, the year his father got the lung diagnosis. He put down half a pack of Camels on the kitchen counter and never picked them up again. Never had one in the house after that day.
He was stubborn. Tell Greg to find his reason and keep it in front of him. Harold's was his father's X-ray. That was enough.
Do we have any family history with drinking that I should know about for Sophie's medical forms?

On my side: my mother's brother Walter. He drank heavily for years and his liver gave out in 1982. He was fifty-nine years old. Mother's side only, as far back as I know. Your father's side I can't speak to.
Ok. I'll note it on the maternal side.
Uncle Walter. 1982. That's the relevant entry.
How did the appointment go? Did Dr. Nguyen look at the CGM data?
She was pleased. Said the number is holding where we want it. No change to the metformin dose for now.
That is a relief. The summer bump scared me a little. Good that the extra 5 mg she added in August seems to have settled things.
It took a couple of months but yes. The CGM helps too — I can see when something I ate is not agreeing with me.
Did the water bill go through online? I saw you had a question about it last week.
It went through on the 24th. I confirmed it on the bank site and wrote it in the notebook same day.
Mom you don't need to write it down too if you can see it on the screen.
I have been keeping that register since 1968. It is not going anywhere. The computer could be wrong.
TCM had The Searchers on. I have probably seen it a dozen times.
The photography holds up. Monument Valley every time. Ford knew what he was doing with that landscape.
I remember you watching Stagecoach with us on Friday nights growing up.
Those are the ones. Ford understood something about this country. Your father loved them too.
Did February come out heavy with the heating bills?
About $3,200. Gas was up and I had that co-pay and the plow twice. That is the heavy end for me.
That is a lot for one month.
It is, but I budget for it. March will come back down to around twenty-four hundred. April will be light, maybe nineteen hundred. It balances.
You always have a number for every month. I should learn from you.
My niece keeps sending me links to turmeric capsules for the knees. Have you ever tried anything like that?
I tried acupuncture once in 2010 for a shoulder problem. Three sessions. It did not hurt and it did not help. That was the end of that.
What about the supplements, the herbal kind?

Dr. Nguyen told me years ago that anything botanical can interact with my blood pressure pill. I keep it to the four she approved — vitamins and aspirin. No herbals. I would rather have a cup of ginger tea and use the heating pad.
Mom, I set up that Spotify playlist for you — the one with the hymns and some light classical. It's on the tablet.
That was thoughtful of you. I looked at it. I think I'll leave it alone. The radio in the kitchen does just fine for me.
You can just tap the big button! Lily uses it constantly.
I'm sure Lily does. I prefer WUOM in the mornings and whatever comes on PBS in the evenings. That's enough music for me.
Ok Mom. Just wanted to make it easier.
Marco found a genealogy record for an Otto Meyer who arrived at Baltimore in 1908 — age 22, from the Grand Duchy of Baden. Could that be your grandfather?

That would be him. Grandpa Otto always said he came from a town near Freiburg. The dates fit — he'd have been young, maybe 21 or 22. He settled in Toledo first then moved to the Adrian area for factory work.
He was a union man. UAW later, once the plants organized. Grandpa Otto believed very strongly in that. Father followed him into it.
The labor roots run deep. I love it.
Did your father speak German at all?

He understood it — Grandpa Otto spoke it at home when Father was small. But Father stopped speaking it around 1942 or 1943. He and his brothers just stopped. Nobody discussed it much at the time. It was the war.
That happened in so many German-American families. Did Grandpa Otto keep speaking it?

Not in public. Maybe a word or two at home privately. By the time I was born in 1940 it was just gone from the household. There was nothing left of it. I never heard a sentence of German in our house growing up.
Did the gas bill drop yet from the December-February highs?
Not yet. February was still $250. I expect it to come down to $40 or so by May. It always does once the furnace stops running overnight.

I budget for it every January. December through February I set aside for the high gas. The property tax hits July and December, the homeowner insurance is in May, and the car insurance I renew April and October.
Did you watch the Sunday morning shows today? The senator was on Face the Nation.
I watched both. Meet the Press first, then Face the Nation. They had three different guests on infrastructure and I took notes.
I wanted to tell Daniel. He tracks water infrastructure policy.
Mom I have a nice blazer that might fit you. It is a size 8 petite. Want me to bring it in April?
A petite might work now. I am at five-three and about 140. Used to be five-five so things fit differently than they did. Bring it and we will see.
I figured. Sophie is five-four so you two are close enough that I thought it might work.
The weight has been steady at 140 for several years. The inches are the newer change. Dr. Nguyen said it is normal past eighty.
My mother's social worker described her using a bunch of demographic categories that felt so clinical. Did anyone ever do that to you?

I imagine I'd come out about as predictable as anyone in this county. Born here, married here, raised children here, still here. Sixty-two years in one house. Harold gone, still going. There's probably a box on a form that covers it.
I know. But the box isn't wrong either. Long marriage, three children, long-resident homeowner, widow, still keeping accounts at the senior center. It all lines up rather neatly.
Have you ever seriously thought about moving closer to Kathy?

I've been on this street for sixty-two years. My church membership is sixty-one years. Marjorie and I have been friends since 1972. My accountant Rick Bauer went to Adrian High a few years after me. The woman who does my hair, Donna at Main Street Salon, has done it since 1988. I am the town in a way. Moving would mean starting over at eighty-five and I don't see why.
WEMU had some good old-time music this afternoon. Did you catch it?
I had it on while I knitted. They played two Carter Family songs. Wildwood Flower and Will the Circle Be Unbroken. I could have listened all evening.
The Carter Family is the one you always come back to.
Always. My mother had those 78s. I have been listening to them since I was six years old.
Are you still thinking about the Washtenaw class?
I looked at the senior audit program again this week. The business administration certificate. If I do three more courses I would have it. I want to finish before I cannot.
Energy mostly. The night class in 1974 nearly did me in at fifty-six credits. But I have been thinking about it seriously.
Do it. I will come to the graduation. 🌱
Good morning. Did you make it to Walgreens before your walk? I know Monday mornings can be tight.
Got there at seven sharp. They had the 90-day ready, so I was in and out in ten minutes. Took them at 7:15 like always.
Good. I worry when you push the refill date. Dr. Nguyen was very clear about not letting that one lapse.
I know, I know. It has been the same drill since 1998. I am not going to forget now.
Mom, I want to go over the spring budget with you before the furnace estimate comes in. Are you comfortable sharing what's coming in?

We've done this before. The pension from Ford through the UAW is $2,700 give or take. Social Security comes in two parts now — my own and the survivor share from Harold's — that's about $1,950 together. And then the RMD from the IRA, which comes in quarterly but averages out to maybe $800 a month. So just under $5,500 gross coming in every month.
It has been. I don't plan to make any changes.
Your financial advisor, Pete Hendricks, called me to confirm you don't want to move anything into the income ladder he suggested. Should I tell him you're sticking with the current allocation?

Tell him yes. I don't touch what's working. Harold and I paid off the mortgage in 1987 — twelve years early. We put every spare dollar into that house rather than take vacations. I have never borrowed money for anything except the original mortgage. I don't need a ladder. I need not to lose what I have.
I don't need upside. I need the floor to hold. There's a difference.
How did it go without the Tuesday walk? Was the rerouting too much?
I was off all morning. I kept thinking it was a different day. By lunch I was fine but the first two hours I did not like it.
I know. I reminded myself what Harold used to say — that I would survive a change in the weather. He was right. I went ahead and rearranged the crossword to after lunch and that helped.
Good for you. Dad would be proud.
Did you put your aids in before church this Sunday? Pastor Jim spoke quietly the whole time and I could barely follow.
I did. Left one has been a little scratchy lately — I think it needs a cleaning. I missed some of the second scripture.
Take it to Audiology before bridge Tuesday. Better to hear Ruth's complaints clearly than not at all.
Ha. Yes the left has always been the one that needed more attention. I will call Dr. Weston's office this morning.
You look better today at church. Last two Sundays you were somewhere else.
I was. February does this to me. It has been this way since Harold died. Kathy came and stayed and it helped. It has lifted now.
I know. Ken's January does the same to me. I have learned to just name it and wait.
That is exactly what I do. I do not take anything for it — I tried to explain that to Dr. Nguyen and she agreed that as long as I can still function and it resolves, we leave it alone.
There is a millage vote next month. Are you going to vote on it?
I vote on every election. Millage, school board, primary, general — every single one. I have voted in every election since 1962. I missed two because of the flu and I still feel bad about those.
That is remarkable. You have voted in how many?
About a hundred and twenty, I figure. Maybe more if I count the special elections.
Did you see what I posted in the Ypsilanti quilting group today?
I check Facebook after lunch, after the crossword. I saw it. The barn quilt pattern is lovely. I will try it.
You have been in that group for a while. Are you still in the Saline Senior Center one too?
Both groups. The quilting one is more active. I post there maybe once a month when I finish something. You got me onto Facebook in 2011 and I have stayed for those two things.
Did you talk to Richard about the gifts again this year?

Yes. He confirmed the annual exclusion amount and I will give the same amount to all three of you again. Third year in a row. He says as long as I stay under the limit there are no forms and no tax implications.
You really do not have to.
Richard suggested it three years ago as a way to move some of the estate while I can see you enjoy it. It is good financial sense and it makes me happy.
Mom I want to go over your monthly bills when I come Sunday. Just to make sure nothing is going up without you noticing.

I know my bills, Kathy. Property tax runs about $800 a month the way I divide it. The Medicare supplement and Part D together are around $310. Utilities around $220, groceries around $350, gas for the car $40, car insurance $85.
That is $1,400 a year due in May. I put aside $120 a month for it. And the tithe is $200 a month to the church.
Okay. You really do have it all in your head.
In my head and in the notebook.
Lily got a ticket last week — she was doing 48 in a 35 on the way home from school. Rebecca is mortified.

I remember the feeling. I got pulled over in 1978 coming down M-52 just outside Chelsea. I was going too fast — Harold had the kids and I was late getting back from Adrian. The officer was polite. I paid the fine and that was the end of it. One in my whole life.
I had no idea you ever got a ticket!
I don't advertise it. Tell Lily it happens once and then you learn to watch the speedometer.
Did you see that article going around about supplements and kidney function? My niece sent it.
I saw something like it. I looked it up on CDC.gov first and then asked Kathy — she had already read the Consumer Reports piece on the same topic. Between the two of them I feel settled.
That is a sensible approach. I end up going down rabbit holes on random websites.
Dr. Nguyen is always my final word. She told me years ago to stick to CDC, Consumer Reports, and PBS NewsHour for anything health-related. Random websites are not in my rotation.
Did you hear that pair of cardinals in the oak this morning? Male and female both. That is the earliest I have seen them back.
I did not notice. Are you feeding them?
Sunflower seed in the feeder by the window. I have a cedar waxwing too, first of the year. I note these things.
Pat's nephew is apparently in real trouble with the bottle. She's heartbroken about it.

I'm sorry to hear it. My Uncle Walter went that way. Mother's brother. He died of it in 1982 — liver failure. He was fifty-nine. Mother always said Walter was the smartest of her brothers and it just broke her to watch him come apart. I think about Walter when I hear these stories.
It's a cruel thing. The family watches and can't stop it.
That's exactly it. Walter went fast at the end. Pat should know it sometimes goes that way.
Pat said she's been watching that network — you know the one — and coming to bridge with all sorts of claims about the election. How do you handle her?

I don't watch it and I've told Pat I don't. I find it has no interest in being accurate, which is the only standard I hold a news source to. I'm not going to argue with Pat about it but I won't pretend it's a legitimate news organization either.
Ruth just changes the subject whenever it comes up.
That's probably wiser. I've said my piece once and now I just play cards.
Did Rob come yesterday? We had that wet snow.
He was here by 7:15. Driveway was clear before I even had my coffee.
Good. I texted him to check on you when I saw the forecast. He said he adds Lombardy Dr to his Thursday round automatically now.
Forty dollars well spent. I wrote it in the ledger. No complaints from me.
How are the knees after the cold?
Stiff but fine. I stayed in until the salt worked. Did not go out and test my luck.
Sophie's fiance Rafael speaks Spanish at home with his parents. They want to do part of the rehearsal dinner in Spanish. Is that okay with you, Mom?

Of course it is. I will follow along as best I can. I don't speak a word of Spanish, as you know, but I'm not going to be the one to make it complicated. I'll ask Keisha to sit near me and give me the sense of things if I get lost.
That's sweet of you Mom. It means a lot.
Tell Sophie I am looking forward to every bit of it, Spanish included.
Mom Caleb wants to learn to play cards when he comes up. Can you teach him something?
Euchre. I will teach him euchre. That is how we started in Adrian. Your father and I played our first night together with euchre.
I forgot that. I did not know that was your first date.
It was not a date officially. We were at his cousin's kitchen table in Adrian and somebody needed a fourth. That is how it started.
Mom, I was rereading some old letters and found the one where Dad wrote about the 2008 primaries. Did you save yours?
Mixed. I put out two mugs on the counter this morning. I do that still, six and a half years later. I've stopped trying to train myself out of it.
Is it sad when it happens?
I have a box in the closet shelf. I remember that year very clearly. Your father and I were both registered Republican at the time and we both changed our registration before November.
That must have felt like a big step.
A little. But it also feels right. Your father used to hum when he was working on something. The house has been very quiet since he left. The two cups are a way of keeping a place set, I suppose.
Kathy told me about the workshop last February. How are you feeling a year out from that?
It felt overdue. I'd been pulling both ways since 2000 honestly. By 2016 I had re-registered Independent. I'm still there. I vote the person, not the column.
I sometimes wonder what would have happened if we'd stayed in Adrian or gone somewhere else in '64.
Where did you first learn QuickBooks? You seemed to pick it up faster than anyone I know.
You always have. I love you for it.

Better than I expected. That ten-day stretch before it was the hardest I'd had since the first year. Kathy came up and we cleared it out. His tools went to the VFW. His coveralls I kept. I hadn't been in that room in five years before that.
We were in your grandmother's attic in Adrian with two small children and Harold's supervisor said come to Saline. We came. You were barely walking. Kathy was two. We didn't overthink it.
It sounds like it needed to happen.
Marco asked how you'd describe your political identity. He's been thinking about how to explain you to his parents.
And you've been there sixty-two years.
I kept books by hand for your father's shop for twenty-six years. 1966 to 1992. Small-engine repairs. I issued 1099 forms myself, tracked parts inventory, did the quarterly reconciliations.
It did. February 2025. I think of it as a before-and-after.
Sixty-two. I doubt we'll make it sixty-three but I'm going to try.
I never knew it went back that far.

Tell Marco's parents I grew up calling myself a Rockefeller Republican — after Nelson Rockefeller. Moderate, pragmatic, pro-civil rights, fiscally careful. I was registered Republican until 2016. Now I'm Independent. I vote the person. My values haven't moved much; the parties around me have.
Best years it brought in about $3,000, in the eighties dollars. Not much, but I kept every receipt. Good practice.
It's accurate. It's not more complicated than that.
I was thinking about that conversation in 1986, the one in the kitchen. I know it changed things.

It did change things, and I want you to know I have never once regretted how your father and I handled it. You were twenty-two. You came home from Michigan State and you told us at the kitchen table and your father stood up and hugged you. That's the whole story.
I know. I just wanted to say thank you again.
Four years later we were at Detroit Pride together. That was 1990 and I wore sensible shoes and your father carried a sign. Don't thank us for what parents are supposed to do.
Ready for the Sunday crossword when I get there? I am bringing salad.
I saved it. I did not touch the Sunday one this morning. The daily I already finished at nine.
You do it every morning. How often do you finish?
Almost always. I only leave blanks when I can not verify the answer. Sunday ones I save so we can do them together.
Tom and I were watching a documentary about the Willow Run bomber plant. Tom said the name sounded familiar — isn't that connected to your mother?

Mother worked there from 1942 to 1945. She riveted the wing panels on the B-24s. She took a bus from Adrian to Ypsilanti for three years on rotating shifts. She kept her ID card from the plant until she died.
I had no idea it was wing panels specifically.
I have been thinking about whether your emergency fund is still in the right place. Have you moved anything recently?
She was very specific about it when she told the story. She was proud of it. She went back to being a homemaker in 1945 when Father came home, but those three years stayed with her her whole life.
No. The money market at Bank of Ann Arbor is at $42,000. The Vanguard brokerage I do not touch unless Richard tells me. The Chase CDs ladder I roll as they mature.
And you are still putting some aside each month?
About $200 a month from the Social Security and pension after expenses. Goes into the money market first.
Mom, Sophie is doing a module on coverage structures for seniors. She asked if she could use your setup as an example — anonymized. Is that okay?

That is fine. Tell her: the base is covered by what they take from my Social Security automatically. Then I pay Blue Cross Plan G and the Part D separately — about $230 combined each month. Altogether it runs about $400 a month.
She will love that. She said Plan G is the gold standard for supplemental.
I have had no gaps in coverage since I turned 65. It is worth every dollar.
Sophie has her whole wedding planning on Instagram. Do you want me to show you how to make an account so you can follow it?
No thank you. You can show me the photos when you visit. I am not getting on Instagram.
What about TikTok? Lily is on it.
Absolutely not. I have Facebook for the two groups and that is quite enough. TikTok, Instagram — I do not need any of those.
Still on for 8? I can push to 8:15 if you need more time.
I am ready. Pills were at 7:15, oatmeal at 7:30. Nothing moves my 7:15.
I know. I have never known you to run late on that.
Thirty years of the same. Dr. Nguyen asked once what my secret was and I said a pill organizer and a very reliable clock.
The senior center is showing a new app for medication reminders. Might be useful for you.

I've seen the flyer. I won't use something new until someone I trust has looked at it. Can you check it out and tell me what you think? You work in healthcare. If you say it's straightforward, I'll try it.
Did you drive or walk to the library yesterday?
I'll look it over this week.
Thank you. That's all I need.
Walked. It was clear and I wanted the mile. A mile to the library and back is a good morning.
How close is the pond from your house?
Mill Pond is four blocks. I can see the top of the big willow from the back garden. I could walk to it and back before breakfast if I wanted.
Book club picked The Women by Kristin Hannah next month. Have you read it?
I did not. I have been finishing Ruthie Fear — it is not quite what I like. I prefer the ones set back farther. Civil War, the frontier, the Depression. Give me something with history in it.
The Women has a historical setting, Vietnam era.
That counts. Put me down. I will read it before the meeting.
How do you find QuickBooks for the senior center work? Is it overkill for a small nonprofit?
I thought it might be when Linda asked me to use it. I had only ever done paper ledgers. But I have been on it since 2022 and now I prefer it. The grant tracking is much cleaner online.
How long did it take to learn?
About six weeks before I trusted it. The logic is the same as any ledger. I just had to learn where they hid everything.
So are you getting the new behind-the-ear ones? Dr. Feldman said they're much smaller.
He did say that. I told him these work fine and I'm not replacing them just because something smaller exists. People can see the aids and that's perfectly all right with me.
The smaller ones might be more comfortable though.
I'll think about it. But I'm not spending Medicare's money on cosmetics. New domes and fresh batteries and I'll be fine for bridge on Tuesday.
You redid your quilt block again?
The corner seam was off by a quarter inch. I am not presenting it at guild looking like that.
I would. I measure a board four times before I cut it. That is just how I am.
I know, I know. Harold always said the same thing. Bring it Tuesday and let me see.
You are limping again. Do not tell me it is nothing. I watched you come up the steps at bridge.
The right hip was bad this morning. I took two extra-strength at breakfast and it helped some but not all the way.
You cannot live on Tylenol forever... Did Dr. Nguyen not have another option?
She says walking is actually the best thing for it. So I walk and I take the Tylenol when it flares. Three times a week on average.
Did Linda bring up the stipend again?
She mentioned it at the end of the meeting. I told her the same thing I told her last time. No.
Why not? You do real work. You deserve something.
If they paid me I would feel obligated. Right now I show up because I want to. The moment money enters it becomes something else.
I will never fully understand that.
You do not have to. I understand it.
Lovely. The Lenten anthems are really coming together. I sat near the side aisle so I could hear the altos properly.
You go every Wednesday and still don't sing with them. You should join!
I am perfectly happy right where I am. My voice is best kept to myself. Listening is its own gift.
My granddaughter is thinking about working as a poll worker this fall. Do you remember what it was like?
I did it for eight cycles at precinct 3 in Saline. 2004 through 2018. You get there at five in the morning and you leave at nine at night. It is long but it is real service.
2018 was my last one. Harold needed more of my attention by then. I am glad I did it as long as I did.
Good walk today. You were moving well.

I watch the NewsHour and I read the papers and then I put it down. But I watch with a heaviness I didn't carry in the eighties. In 1988 I had my candidate and I voted and I trusted the system to work. Now I vote and then I hold my breath. That's different.
I want it to pull together. I tell myself it has before. I'm not sure it always has but I tell myself that.
How did the grant committee Zoom go this morning?
Fine. Brian's instructions are still on the monitor. I do not need them anymore but I keep them there anyway.
He taught you Zoom in 2020 right?
He wrote it all out by hand. Step by step. His handwriting is terrible but I can read it. Six years later it is still on the monitor.
Knitting. I have been at it since eight. The baby blanket for Sophie is about half done.
Every evening. It is the best part of the day when the house is quiet.
Sophie asked who your doctor is — for her paperwork notes on your wellness picture.
Dr. Patricia Nguyen, IHA Saline on Russell Street. She has been mine since 2016. Tell Sophie she can put Dr. Nguyen down as the one who knows everything.
Perfect. She said having a consistent primary over many years is a huge factor in older-adult outcomes.
Yes. I was just reading that the hospital is doing a survey on patient demographics and they need volunteers. You'd know more about that than I would.
Ha yes. It's for the equity audit. They're trying to understand where the gaps are in who gets served.
I'd be a boring data point for them. Elderly, long-resident, about as ordinary a Washtenaw County background as you can imagine.
That's actually exactly what they're documenting. Ok, see you outside.
Do you remember talking about the Floyd case on our walk a few years ago? You said something about institutional patterns and I didn't quite understand at the time.
I remember. You said it was the first time you'd really sat with it all the way through.
I cried, which surprised me. And I called Daniel that night. It was a turning point in how I approach these conversations. I read more now before I say anything.
That's a real thing. It matters.
Did Emma get back to Grand Valley okay?
She left Sunday after lunch. Texted me when she got to the highway. The guest room needs the duvet aired out again for May.
She said she has a week off in late May. I told her the room is hers whenever she needs it.
How did the tax appointment go?
Good. Richard had everything ready in forty minutes. I paid the $250, same as every year. He has done my taxes since 1988.
Is he still in that same office on Fourth Ave?
Same building since 1992. I have been going there for thirty-eight years. I do not see any reason to change.
Every inning. They won and I stayed up past ten for it. I have been a Tigers fan since 1960. I am not going to stop now.
Who is your favorite on the current roster?
I like the young pitchers. The starting rotation looks better than last year. I listen on the radio when it is on at the same time as something I want to watch on TV.
Do you still have the old business ledgers from Dad's shop?
In the filing cabinet. Every year from 1966 through 1992. I kept them in case Richard ever needed them for something.
That is amazing. Nobody throws anything away.
I was the bookkeeper. It was my record. The IRS had twenty-six years of clean filings from that shop.
Mom I saw a Wyeth print at the antique store near the market. Do you want me to get it?
Which one? I already have the Christina's World card on the refrigerator. If it is Distant Thunder or Wind from the Sea I would put it in the hall.
It looks like fields. A farmhouse. Very quiet.
That sounds like Wyeth. Get it. You know what I like.
Marco was curious about the Cintron side for the ancestry project. Is it Puerto Rico on Dad's father's line?

Yes. Harold's father Ernesto was born in Ponce. His mother was German-American from the Toledo area, which is how Ernesto ended up in Michigan. Harold was born right here in Saline and never lived in Puerto Rico. The name came from Ernesto's family.
So we're a quarter Puerto Rican by blood but fully Midwestern by every other measure.
That's a fair summary. Your grandmother Meyer used to joke that the Cintron name was the most interesting thing about us.

Did you ever feel like you missed out by not finishing college, Mom?
More than I want to admit. I had the afternoon blocked out and then suddenly I had nothing in that slot. It is silly.

Sometimes. I graduated from Adrian High in 1958 and I was admitted to Siena Heights that fall — it was a business administration program run by the Dominican Sisters. I did two years and then the choice about Harold came up and I chose Harold.
It is not silly. It is just how you are wired.
But you kept working with numbers your whole life anyway.
Your father used to tease me about it. I am working on it. I moved the quilt session up and kept going. Progress.
That is real progress, Mom. I mean it. 🌱
I did. Siena Heights gave me enough foundation to keep the books at the senior center for twenty years. Sister Mary Agnes always said I had the mind for it and just not the finishing time.
Sister Mary Agnes was the one who told me I should sit the CPA exam. That was 1960. She said the firm in Ann Arbor had taken on two women the previous year and she thought I had the ability.

I chose Harold. I've never said that was a wrong choice. But I have thought about Sister Mary Agnes's face when I told her. She was disappointed in a way she was too gracious to show. I think about that when I talk to Emma about finishing school first.
Did you ever come close to finishing a degree?
You always bring Sister Mary Agnes up when you talk to Emma.

I took one night class at Washtenaw Community College in 1974 — bookkeeping refresher, Tuesday evenings at the Ann Arbor campus. One semester. That was the extent of it after Siena Heights. I always thought about going back and never quite did.
One class in 1974 and that was it.
That was it. But it was enough to get me the job keeping books at the senior center in 1980.
Marco asked me what you actually care about most, when you strip everything else away. I said family first. Was I right?
I will FaceTime you Sunday for the regular call instead of Zoom. Marco wants to show you the new fig tree.

Yes. Family is first and nothing is close. After that, keeping your word. Then order — my own house and affairs in order. After that, service to other people — the senior center, the church treasurer role. Then faith, which holds all the rest together. And last, keeping a sense of proportion about things. Not letting any single problem become the whole picture.
That is fine. FaceTime works well on my phone. Make sure Marco holds it steady this time — last month it was all motion.
I've had time to think about it.
Ha. I will hold it. See you Sunday.
When you think about what you still want to do, what comes up?

Finish the accounting certificate. I've been saying it for years and I want to do it before I can't. See Emma and Lily settled on a path before I go. Keep this house running on my own so nobody has to carry me. Be remembered as someone who paid attention and showed up — for you, for the town, for the people who needed something. Not famous. Just present.
It got clearer after Harold. You start to think about what you actually have left to do.
I was reading something about coming-of-age in the 1980s and thought about Daniel's year. Do you ever talk about it with him?

We talked about it tonight actually — he brought up 1986. It was a hard year for many reasons but Daniel telling us was not one of the hard parts. It was one of the good parts, even though I know he was frightened.
I remember he was scared. I was twenty-four and I didn't fully understand what he must have been feeling.
1986. He was twenty-two. We did the right thing and I'm glad we knew it at the time.
Mom are you still up? The Michigan women just won.
I watched every minute. That last quarter was something. I am very proud of that team.
Tom had no idea you followed them. I told him you have watched every season.
They deserve the attention. I have been watching them since before they had a real broadcast budget.
Sophie called me — she is doing a case study on follow-up imaging protocols. She asked about your history and I told her it was your story to share.
That is fine. She can call me. The short version is: lumpectomy 2005, radiation, then every May for the imaging. Dr. Nguyen has been very consistent about it.
She will love talking to you. She said early-detection follow-up protocols have some of the best long-term outcomes in the literature.
I was fortunate they caught it when they did. Kathy is driving me to IHA in May for the annual imaging.
How does the DAF work on your end? Do you control what it gives to?

I recommend the recipients and the amounts. It grows in the fund until I say so. Richard set it up through the Vanguard account distributions. I use it so the charitable money goes out cleanly without tax complications.
Smart. And you do not have to decide every year what to give.
I decide. I just do not have to write a dozen checks.
Did you end up rolling the Chase CD or moving the money somewhere else?
Rolled it. The rate was still decent. Richard looked at the Vanguard side last fall and left it alone. I am not in the market for drama.
Smart. The money market at Bank of Ann Arbor still healthy?
It is. Still at forty-two thousand after the furnace. I put back about two hundred a month.
Did you see the thing circulating about the water fluoridation? Several people in our neighborhood group posted it.

I did. I replied to two of them with the Washtenaw water authority page. One person thanked me and one person argued. I'm used to it. I'd rather be the one who says something than let it circulate unchecked.
I prefer consistent. The wrong information doesn't stop traveling just because you're polite about it.
Did you end up rearranging your Thursday walk? You've been very consistent about that.

I did not. I offered to move bridge once — once, and only because Marjorie asked. That was years ago. My Thursday walk and my Tuesday bridge are not negotiable. Now, if Keisha asked me to do something for Brian and it fell on a Tuesday, that might be different. But that would be about her, not the activity.
So the schedule is for you but the exceptions are for people you love.
The city is doing a tree planting program on Maple Ave. Did you see the notice?
I saw it. I am signing up for one in the back corner. I have been meaning to replace the old birch.
I keep meaning to ask — do you use any chemicals on your garden?
None. Compost only. I have never put a pesticide on this land. You cannot give the soil something and then take it back with poison. That is not stewardship.
Brian and Keisha's anniversary is coming up in June — their fifth. Are you planning to send something?

I have it on the calendar. June 12th. Five years — 2021. I'll send a card with a note and probably a check. That wedding changed how I look at a lot of things, Kathy. I'm grateful they married when they did.
Keisha has been wonderful for the whole family.
She has. And patient with all of us.
I called at seven and you did not pick up. Everything all right?
I was at my 7:15. I cannot answer the phone during that fifteen minutes. I have the pill organizer out, the water, the whole lineup. It is the one thing I ask people not to interrupt.
Understood. I forget sometimes. You have kept that schedule for as long as I have known you.
It was the rule my doctor set and I have never broken it. If I break the schedule I lose track of what I have taken.
Do you remember when you first started at the center? I keep forgetting how it happened.
Forty dollars. That is how it happened. They were short forty dollars in the accounts and no one could explain it. I spotted the transposed number. Linda asked me to come back.
And now you do the whole thing.
Forty dollars and a transposed digit started all of it. That is worth remembering.
I picked up new slacks at the Ann Arbor Goodwill — two pairs for $11. You should come next time.
I should. I need new walking shoes before summer. Eleanor says my current ones are worn through at the heel and she is probably right. But the rest of my wardrobe is holding up fine.
Shoes are the one thing you shouldn't scrimp on at our age.
I agree. Everything else I scrimp on without apology.
Pat keeps trying to get you to come to the Friday social. You always say no.

The Friday social has no fixed structure. People arrive when they arrive and conversation goes wherever. I don't mind conversation but I like to know what I'm walking into. Give me bridge — fourteen hands, a partner, a score, a clear outcome. The social feels like noise to me.
You're not wrong about the noise.
I can do a party for two hours with a purpose. Open-ended mingling is harder for me than I let on.
I talked to my niece about her aunt with the memory issues. She said she always corrects her and it always ends in tears.
Pat wants to play euchre next week instead of bridge. Thoughts?
I have no objection. I grew up on euchre. I could still play it in my sleep.

I stopped correcting Maggie two years ago. She told me something about Mother last Tuesday that happened forty years before it actually did and I just said 'I remember that.' There's nothing to be gained. She's in her own world now and it's a world where people she loves are still around.
That takes a certain peace to do.
I will explain it. Every Michigan kid knew how to play it before they knew how to drive. Ruth will pick it up in ten minutes.
It does. She was my first friend. I have enough peace left to give her that much.
Good morning. Checked the carrots and the cabbage seedlings. Everything is coming up well for this early.
That early? You are out there already?
Seven o'clock, same as every day from now until October. The tomatoes I started inside in February are ready to harden off in another two weeks.
Send me photos when the carrots come in. My dahlias are barely poking up yet. 🌱
I will. The rosemary made it through winter again. I check it every morning.
Sore arm today? I saw you heading to Walgreens yesterday.
A little. Got the flu shot. I do it every year without fail.
Smart. Did you get the updated COVID one last fall too? I kept putting mine off.

September 2023. That was my fourth one — original two in 2021, booster that same fall, then the updated one in 2022, and the 2023. I keep a list in the notes section of my calendar so I do not lose track.

My accounting teacher in 1960. She was the one who said I should get a degree and a CPA license. She was right. I made a different choice.
Only when something reminds me. Signing the WCC catalog page. Sending Linda's board report. Not with regret exactly. More like... I see the road I did not take.
Emma is doing a whole section on what life was like for family members as teenagers. Would you write a paragraph for her project?

I'll tell her when we talk Sunday. At sixteen I was living at home in Adrian, both parents were married and working, Maggie and the boys were all home too. It was 1956 and we had the same house we'd had since I was small. Nothing dramatic to report, which was itself a kind of gift.
She will love that. The normalcy of it.
Were you close to your grandmother when you were young?

Very close. Grandma Elsa lived with us from about 1953 until 1961 when she passed. She had her own room off the kitchen. She taught me to knit and to keep a neat account book. I was thirteen when she moved in and I spent a lot of time with her in the evenings.
That's a long time to share a house.
Eight years. It shaped how I thought about taking care of elders. You keep them close if you can. Maggie and I both got that lesson from Grandma Elsa being there.
When did you lose your dad, Mom? Emma wants to include that for Grandpa Meyer's entry.

1974. I was thirty-four. Kathy you were twelve. He died in March — I was just beginning that night class at Washtenaw. It hit hard because there was no warning. He'd retired from Bohn in 1969 and had five good years, then gone.
I remember the house being very quiet for a long time after.
It was. Mother had been expecting more years. We all had.
Mom, when did you graduate high school? Sophie is asking for the family education table she's doing.
June 1958, Adrian High School. Then Siena Heights College for two years, 1958 to 1960. I didn't finish there. Tell Sophie to put 'some college' for me.
Sophie also wants birth years for you, Dad, and us three kids.
Tell her: Kathy, 1962. Daniel, 1964. You, 1968. Your father was born in 1937 and I was born in 1940. We can cover four decades between the five of us.
Lily asked if she could call you about college. She said you always know what to say.

Tell her to call Sunday after 2. I'll tell her the same thing I tell Emma: finish the degree before you think about anything else. The rest of life will wait. The door on the education doesn't always stay open.
I just want her to have what I didn't get to finish.

Good. I always forget you use that app. Most people your age just call.
I prefer writing over talking on the phone with a medical office. I have it in writing and I can check back.
Three robins on the lawn this morning. The first robin is always the best day in April.
In the back. I have the feeder set up year-round. Sometimes I just sit at the kitchen window with my coffee and watch.
I have a Anna's hummingbird in the figs right now. I will send a photo. 🌱
There are some good quilt shops on Etsy. Have you ever tried it?
I have not. I use Missouri Star and that is enough for fabric. I buy through websites I have an account on. I do not buy through apps or social media.
Three days. I have been ordering from them for four years. Same website, same account.
I had to re-hem three dresses this spring. Lost two inches since 2018.
I know the feeling. I was five-five most of my life and now I am five-three. Two inches gone. Dr. Nguyen measured me last March — one-forty on the scale, five-three on the tape.
I feel it in the mirror. My slacks all pool. I had three pairs taken in.
The guild newsletter asked about member crafts. Are you quilt-only or do you do other things?
Quilting is the main one. I also crochet, mostly gifts. Currently I have a quilt in progress and a crocheted baby blanket. Different tools on the table depending on the evening.
I don't know how you can read those WSJ opinion pieces and not throw something.

I don't read them every day. A few times a month at most. I find they keep me honest about what the other side actually thinks as opposed to the cartoon version. Whether I agree or not is beside the point.
A few times a month is not discipline. It's just curiosity.
Pat sent something from Facebook about PBS defunding. She seemed genuinely worried.

I sent her the actual PBS budget link. PBS has been my most reliable source for fifty years. If they're defunded I'll be genuinely worried about what's left. The NewsHour is the one television program I trust completely. Facebook is the one platform I mostly don't.
I feel the same about PBS.
It's not complicated — some sources have earned it and some haven't. PBS has. Facebook's information environment has not.
Some of my coworkers are talking about refinancing to pull equity out of their homes for renovations. Does that ever tempt you?
No. I paid this house off in 1999 and I have no intention of putting debt back on it. I do not borrow. The credit card is paid in full every month. The car is paid. That is how I live.
That is a very specific kind of security.
It is the only kind I want.
Marco made dinner to old folk music tonight. Got me thinking of your house growing up.
Your grandmother's Carter Family records. I played them every Sunday. Keep the Skillet Good and Greasy, Can the Circle Be Unbroken. I wore those records out.
I did not know those titles. Do you still have them?
I have the CD versions. The originals are gone. But I still know every word.
My nephew keeps telling me to get on X — which is what they are calling Twitter now. Are you on it?
No. I was never on Twitter and I will not be on X. I do not follow Fox News either. I have PBS and the Ann Arbor News. That is my information and I do not need more sources making noise.
Same. I told him I am sixty-four years past the need to be on everything.
The immigration bill is moving again. Are you following it?

I told you what I think. People who want to build a life here should have a clear path. This country was built on that. Harold's family came from Puerto Rico. My family came from Germany. It is the same story.

You walked to the pond yesterday? That is further than I thought.
It is four blocks. I go when the weather is nice. Library is a mile, I do that at least once a week in good weather. I can still get to most of what I need on foot.

It is one of the reasons I will not leave this house. Everything I need is four blocks or a mile away.

I have the catalog. The certificate program has a senior audit track. Three courses and I would be done. I did one course back in 1974 and I always meant to go back.

I know. I am looking at the fall semester. It matters to me that I finish.

I put it in the quilting group. I do not post much — maybe once a month — but when I finish something I like to share it there.

The Saline Senior Center group and the quilting one. That is all I need from it.

Paid is a different thing. I do not want obligations tied to money at this point in my life. I want to give freely.
The county is recruiting election workers for the fall. Would you ever go back to it?
I worked precinct 3 for eight election cycles. I stopped in 2018. At my age the sixteen-hour day is not realistic anymore.
That is still impressive. Eight cycles is a lot.
It is. I would recommend it to anyone who can manage the hours. The counting at the end is the best part.
I updated my own paperwork with my daughter last week. Have you done yours recently?

I did it with Kathy in January. The dying part I can make my peace with. It's the long middle I don't want — where you're there but not there and someone has to manage every bit of you. I'd rather go like Harold went, honestly. Quick and without a long goodbye.
That's between me and the Lord. The paperwork is for everyone else.

Family. Then: keeping my word no matter what. I would rather be wrong in every other way than break a promise. The rest — order, service, faith, keeping my head on straight — those are the structure around those two.
Keeping your word above even faith?
Faith gives me the foundation. Word is the daily practice of it. They aren't in competition but word is where you can see it.

I hope so. I have to hope so. I can't spend whatever I have left not hoping that it does.
Mariners won today. How are the Tigers doing?
Three and three as of today. Too early to worry. Harold and I had Tigers season schedule on the refrigerator every year since 1962.

I am considering it. I gave in 2020 and 2021 and then I pulled back. I am looking at the budget to see if I have room this cycle.
Brian would appreciate knowing you did.
That is partly why I am thinking about it again.
